author_role: AI source researcher and wording author; no independent acceptance or specialist review claimed

acquisition.lexical_pages: Original Oxford and Collins lexical URLs were opened with the web tool; findings do not depend on search snippets.
acquisition.raw_oxford_supplement: Original Oxford URLs were also fetched directly with PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing. Sense opening tags were extracted from response.Content; SHA256 was computed over response.RawContentStream.ToArray().
acquisition.raw_hash_scope: Hashes identify the independently fetched response body bytes at the recorded retrieval time, not the web-rendered line snapshot and not this JSON artifact.
acquisition.visible_vs_metadata: The Oxford text renderer leaves its headword/sense level icons blank. Rendered selected-sense CEFR labels therefore remain null. Observed HTML cefr/fkcefr attributes are recorded separately without silently replacing rendered labels.
acquisition.corrected_url_selection: Oxford report_1 opened successfully but is the noun page; it was excluded and report_2 was opened for the verb.

current.definition: To put a new or different item in the place of another.
current.example: We need to replace the damaged folder.

entries.selected_sense: Replacing an existing item with another; the damaged-folder example specifically instantiates replacement of a damaged item.

sense_1.scope: one entity serves instead of another

other_senses.scope: one entity serves instead of another

wording_suggestion.definition: To put a new or different item in the place of another.
wording_suggestion.example: We need to replace the damaged folder with a new one.
wording_suggestion.change_note: Retain the natural current definition; the revised original example makes the replacement frame explicit.

ambiguity_or_difficulty_blockers: General definition and damaged-item example span related senses 2 and 3; identify both rather than applying Collins B1+ to every use.
Current A2 has Oxford HTML support, while Collins prints B1+ for general substitution and B1 for damaged-item replacement. Preserve the disagreement for an editorial difficulty decision.
Exclude the put-back sense; it overlaps with return but is not this target.

current.definition: To take or send something back to an earlier place or person.
current.example: Please return the key to reception.

entries.selected_sense: Transitive giving or sending an object back, with a borrowed key as the contextual instance.

selected_sections.scope: borrowed or taken object given or put back

related_section.scope: purchased item taken or sent back to seller

wording_suggestion.definition: To give or send something back to its owner or the place it came from.
wording_suggestion.example: Please return the borrowed key to reception.
wording_suggestion.change_note: Replace the awkward 'earlier place or person' with an explicit object-return relation; borrowed makes the Collins selected sense unambiguous.

ambiguity_or_difficulty_blockers: Do not use Oxford A1 for the intransitive travel sense to label this transitive object sense.
Current A2 is printed for Collins borrowed-object sense; Oxford selected HTML and Shopping topic are b1. Record both.
Do not transfer the Collins A2 borrowed-object label to every purchased-goods return without noting its separate unlabeled sense.

current.definition: To give information about an event, result, or problem to someone responsible.
current.example: Please report the equipment problem to the supervisor.

entries.selected_sense: Communicating observed information, including a workplace problem; the current authority-oriented recipient partly overlaps the separate official-reporting sense.

related_section.heading: crime/accident, etc.
related_section.scope: authority-facing disclosure; related but not primary selected sense

selected_sections.scope: tell people about an occurrence, including reporting an incident to police

other_senses.scope: report on a subject as job or duty

wording_suggestion.definition: To tell someone about an event, result, or problem.
wording_suggestion.example: Please report the equipment problem to the supervisor.
wording_suggestion.change_note: The original shortened definition fits general give-information scope; the existing example supplies the workplace recipient.

ambiguity_or_difficulty_blockers: The current 'someone responsible' restriction blends general information reporting with authority-facing reporting. Either document the narrower workplace scope or use the suggested general definition.
Oxford primary-sense HTML is a2 while Collins primary-sense visible label is B1; neither independently validates the lesson difficulty.
The noun page report_1 and arrival-for-duty sense are excluded.

current.definition: To formally tell someone information they need to know.
current.example: Please notify the team if the meeting time changes.

entries.selected_sense: Formal or official communication of information to someone.

selected_sections.patterns: notify someone of/about something; notify someone that; notify someone

sources.visible_cefr_status: No CEFR label was printed in the selected verb section.

wording_suggestion.definition: To tell someone about something in a formal or official way.
wording_suggestion.example: Please notify the team of the new meeting time.
wording_suggestion.change_note: Original wording clarifies formality and demonstrates the frequent notify someone of something construction.

ambiguity_or_difficulty_blockers: Current A2 is unsupported by these selected-source levels: Oxford explicitly records c1 in HTML and Collins prints no selected CEFR label.
Keep difficulty held unless a directly supported editorial rationale justifies a different lesson level; do not clamp C1 to B2 merely to fit an allowed range.
The visible B2 footer belongs to reasonably and cannot justify a B2 notify decision.

current.definition: To communicate with a person or organization.
current.example: I will contact the supplier about the missing box.

entries.selected_sense: Getting in touch with a person or organization to exchange information.

selected_sections.scope: phone, write, or visit to tell or ask something

wording_suggestion.definition: To communicate with a person or organization.
wording_suggestion.example: I will contact the supplier about the missing box.
wording_suggestion.change_note: The existing definition and example are natural and directly match the selected communication sense; no wording change is necessary.

ambiguity_or_difficulty_blockers: Current A2 matches the Collins selected verb label, while Oxford selected HTML and topic label are b1. Preserve both.
Do not use the Collins B1 noun label or Oxford footer B2 as the verb's selected label.
Contact takes a direct object in the target example; do not introduce an unnecessary 'with' after the verb.

handoff_scope: Wording suggestions are authored proposals only. Parent owns candidate construction, context screening, difficulty policy decisions, independent review, and integration.
